justifications.c1: Independent per-incident figures ≥£2k: Withernsea school £18k fine + £3,939 costs (IEMA, search-confirmed), Suffolk £20k fine, council guidance and OFTEC that clean-up 'regularly' exceeds £20k; Chubb £800k is insurer marketing; but per-site annual loss is unknown because incidents are rare.
justifications.c2: Only national aggregates (~800 oil incidents/yr, 5,308 oil/fuel incidents) and annual OFTEC inspections; researcher found no commercial/institutional leak or bund-failure frequency.
justifications.c3: Annual OFTEC 600A inspections sold by GPT, Tradebe and Crown Oil and liquid-only bund alarms (~£97) are documented; no labour or inspection price found; sources are vendors.
justifications.c4: SI 2001/2954 (legislation.gov.uk) mandates secondary containment above 200 L on commercial/institutional premises; OFTEC (search-confirmed) and broker say clean-up is often not insured and gradual pollution is limited; prosecutions exist, but no rule requires monitoring or records.
justifications.c5: Council estates (Withernsea council surveyed all tanks) and dioceses are inferred buyers; no job adverts or budget evidence (search budget exhausted).
justifications.c6: OFTEC inspectors/environmental contractors visit annually, and oil distributors already sell tank monitors with subscriptions (BoilerJuice search-confirmed, Certa Ireland FoxRadar), though mainly to domestic customers.
justifications.c7: Commoditised level monitoring: Watchman Anywhere £25/yr, BoilerJuice £4.99/month, FoxRadar drop alerts; AFRISO already sells a wireless oil/water bund probe; the combined commercial compliance-pack gap is asserted.
justifications.c8: Level sensing proven at £75 retail and oil/water combination probes are established (AFRISO, Zoeller); no BOM; note search shows BoilerJuice uses an in-tank probe cable, not ultrasonic as the file says.
justifications.c9: Subscriptions accepted but low (£25/yr to ~£60-84/yr); annual OFTEC cycle exists but no statutory record-retention schedule shown.
justifications.c10: EA prosecution reported by IEMA (enforcement), local press and council grant notices, a Singletrack forum thread on insurance liability (domestic); three types present but the forum and much press are domestic rather than commercial.

weakest: Cheap tank monitors with drop alerts (£25-£60/yr) and an existing wireless oil/water bund probe leave little room, and no source shows how often commercial tanks or bunds actually leak.
